headline: RobotLab's arm stops hiding in the mirror: knock-recovery basin fixed
lede: A hard shove could flip the simulated arm into a wrong-basin pose it never escaped — the 4a finding we filed instead of hiding. Measuring the dead zone live found the culprit: no hinge limits, a sensor that breaks when the chain leans, and an error sign that flips exactly where recovery was needed. Three new laws close the basin without touching the tuned routes.

notes.text: #1570 tail: 288-case hammer sweep — light and medium knocks (±0.3/0.6 N·s) now recover 100% of seeds, median 111 ticks, where mirror-basin parking used to be permanent.

Gate 16's deferred recovery assertion is restored: the documented 0.3 N·s tap, both directions, must bring the grasp home — with a mutant-proven sensor-wiring law so the endstop can never silently go blind.

Honest residual: ≥0.8 N·s lateral knocks can hook the fingers on the stand post and jam in-box. The tier response is non-monotonic (0.6 recovers everywhere, 0.8 worst) — real compliant-structure behaviour, documented as the kit's gap, not smoothed over.
